title: St Stephen (26 December)
hookLine: the first martyr's day, and Good King Wenceslas carrying food through the snow

lines: FOOD AND FIREWOOD IN THE SNOW.
cards: A king stands at his window on a freezing night, the snow deep and crisp and even. Below, a poor man is scraping together sticks for a fire. The king turns to his young servant: who is that, and where does he live?
Then he loads up food and drink and firewood, and the two go out into the storm. When the boy can't go on for the cold, the king tells him to step in his footprints, and the ground there is warm.
That's the carol Good King Wenceslas, set on the feast of Stephen, the day after Christmas.

teach.h: WIDOWS LEFT OUT OF THE FOOD.
teach.b: In Acts, the new church in Jerusalem had a problem: some of its widows were being left out when the daily food was handed round.

teach.h: FULL OF FAITH AND OF THE HOLY GHOST.
teach.b: So the apostles asked the community to choose men to take charge of the serving, and first on the list, in the King James Bible: "they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Ghost."

Stephen's job was food: making sure the women nobody noticed got fed. But he also preached and argued, his words angered the city's council, and in the end they dragged him outside the city and stoned him.

Stephen, like the apostles and the people around him, was Jewish; this was a bitter fight inside one community, and Acts tells it that way. His prayers as he dies echo the cross: "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."

teach.h: LAY NOT THIS SIN TO THEIR CHARGE.
teach.b: Then, on his knees: "Lord, lay not this sin to their charge." Acts adds a quiet detail: the men throwing the stones laid their coats at the feet of a young man named Saul, who would later become the apostle Paul.
Tradition calls Stephen the first martyr.
So his feast comes straight after Christmas: the cradle, then the grave. Wenceslas was a real ruler in Bohemia, honored as a saint; the carol is a later story about him.
It puts him out in the snow on Stephen's day carrying food to the poor, exactly what Stephen was chosen to do. In some places, the feast became a day for giving to people in need.

how: Catholic, Anglican and Lutheran churches keep St Stephen's day the day after Christmas, and the Orthodox keep it soon after Christmas on their calendar; in some countries it is a public holiday, and in Britain it is also Boxing Day.

games.q: you're Stephen. the stones are coming. what are your last words?
o: a curse on those who are killing you.
a prayer that God won't hold this against them.
games.why: on his knees, he cried out, "Lord, lay not this sin to their charge" — echoing Jesus on the cross.

practice: Think of who might be left out this week, the way those widows were: someone living alone after the holidays, a neighbor who's been sick, a family that's stretched. Hold one of them in mind, and picture the door you'd knock on.
If you pray, you can hold that person before God by name; if you don't, simply keep them in mind with care.

wordCard.voice: St Stephen. Chosen in Acts to make sure widows were fed, stoned for his preaching, and remembered by tradition as the first martyr, the day after Christmas.
